findings.text: follow-on: dispatch() supplies launch_instant to _compose_dispatch_prompt, but no test pins that wiring - the new parity test injects the instant into the composer directly. A regression dropping the argument leaves the production dispatch prompt with a bare duration and every test green; the resume half of the same feature is covered, so the exposure is one-sided. A test that drives dispatch() and asserts the composed prompt carries a deadline would close it, mirroring test_resume_answers_in_the_same_session.

follow-on: change_lane relaunches a live run from its retained prompt (_lane_prompt) without restating the attempt's fence, so an attempt moved to another lane reads the previous attempt's launch instant and deadline, or none. Section 24 states that a resume restates both for the resumed attempt, and change_lane is a relaunch, in the same declared file; the worker recorded it as a follow-on rather than covering it.

follow-on: the third done-when clause asks that a manifest whose blocker cites an expired time fence before its deadline be reported as a defect rather than a blocker, with the report recorded as a pointer to the owning plan when the audit lives elsewhere. The worker recorded a follow-on naming reckon/crew/reports.py::audit_manifest, a module rather than a plan pointer, and produced no report; outside this node's write scope, so it is carried as a follow-on with the pointer the worker left, but the clause is not fully discharged.

The declared negative control (bare duration restored in the FENCE - TIME line) makes the three parity/instant assertions fail: reproduced by this review in a scratch tree, 3 failed / 1 passed, EXIT=1, same three ids as the manifest's red log.

item_verdicts.manifest: status complete; commits e273934d4, e1cba478f, 436d0b93; baseline_suite and after_suite both populated and readable (failure_count 0, failure_ids []); negative_control_log names the red log whose mutation restores the bare duration.

justifications.durability: The guard lives in product source and fails when reverted - reproduced by this review in a scratch tree with the same three ids the manifest declares. The resume path is exercised as production resolves it: test_crew.py::test_resume_answers_in_the_same_session drives crew.resume_plan and asserts the restated fence follows the advice. Two gaps hold the score below full. First, the dispatch-side wiring is unasserted: the new test injects launch_instant into _compose_dispatch_prompt directly, so a regression that stopped dispatch() passing attempt_started_at (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:5741) would leave a real dispatch prompt with a bare duration and no test would fail. Second, change_lane - in the same declared file - relaunches a live run from its original prompt or a bare continuation and never restates the attempt's fence, so a lane-changed attempt measures against the ended attempt's clock or none; the worker declared this as a follow-on rather than covering it.
justifications.evidence: Both arms are complete and readable with full provenance headers. Base (233f442b0, git archive extraction) 1011 passed EXIT=0; head (e1cba478f, worktree head) 1015 passed EXIT=0; each log names its revision, tree, command, module.__file__, dispatch.__file__ and cwd, and both failure_id lists are empty, so the manifest's zero added failures is well-founded. The declared negative control is genuine: this review mutated the FENCE - TIME line back to the bare duration in a scratch copy of the package and reproduced the red log exactly - 3 failed, 1 passed, EXIT=1, the same three ids. This review also re-ran the new test file against the committed content (4 passed, EXIT=0) and the modified resume integration test test_crew.py::test_resume_answers_in_the_same_session (1 passed). One point withheld: the manifest's measurement_module names only the base-arm extraction, not the head run, though the head-arm log itself carries its module.__file__ header, so the fact is not lost.
justifications.fit: time_fence_statement sits in reckon/crew/prompts.py beside compose_prompt, the composer it serves; _restate_time_fence sits in dispatch.py beside _lane_prompt and is called from resume_plan. Names describe the mechanism, docstrings state why (one clock read so prompt and record cannot disagree; a resume restates because the carried prompt was composed for the ended attempt) rather than the incident. It reuses parse_duration from node.py rather than re-parsing budgets. No version suffixes, no plan or ticket identifiers in symbols, no AI attribution. Minor: _utc_instant re-implements the exact rendering of runs._utc_now rather than sharing it, a small duplication that could drift.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The primary done-when is met: the FENCE - TIME line now states the launch instant, the deadline it sets and `date -u`, and dispatch() takes one _utc_now() read that is both the attempt record's launch instant and the instant the prompt states, so record and prompt cannot disagree. The parity test renders a dispatch prompt and a resume advice for one fixed instant/budget and both carry the same deadline. The third clause - a manifest whose blocker cites an expired fence before its deadline reported as a defect rather than a blocker, with a pointer to the owning plan if the audit lives elsewhere - is only partly discharged: the worker recorded it in follow_ons as belonging to reckon/crew/reports.py::audit_manifest, a module rather than a plan pointer, and no report is produced. This is a real but minor gap beside a fully met core.
justifications.scope_discipline: The base..HEAD diff is confined to the node's declared write paths and nothing else: reckon/crew/prompts.py, reckon/crew/dispatch.py, tests/test_crew.py, tests/test_a_time_fence_names_its_clock.py and the evidence fragment. No plan HTML is edited; the fragment leaves plan state to the coordinator. The granted figures directory carries no figure for this node, consistent with a done-when that names only test artifacts. The reviewed worktree is clean at 436d0b93 and the manifest names no foreign path.
